meeting.title: beehiiv intro chat
meeting.summary: Relationship-building call a week after the beehiiv kickoff. Hannah shared context on the team, their subscriber-growth analytics ambitions, and how they used their previous BI tool. No work was agreed — the existing kickoff plan already covers everything discussed.
discussion_flow: How the data team works today
meeting.notes: Purely a get-to-know-you call. All concrete work is already tracked from the kickoff session last week.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: Hannah, lovely to properly meet you. No agenda today — the kickoff covered the plan, so this is just context and getting to know each other.

transcript.speaker: Hannah Ostrowski
transcript.text: Perfect, I prefer these anyway. So — data team of three, counting me, supporting the whole operation.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: Small but mighty. What does the split look like day to day?

transcript.speaker: Hannah Ostrowski
transcript.text: I do the strategy and stakeholder side, and the two analysts split ops and growth. Everyone writes SQL, nobody wants to maintain dashboards by hand.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: You're the classic profile for metrics-as-code then. What were you using before?

transcript.speaker: Hannah Ostrowski
transcript.text: A pile of notebooks and one very haunted spreadsheet that runs the weekly ops review. Everyone's a little afraid of it.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: The haunted spreadsheet is a rite of passage. Retiring it is usually the emotional milestone of these projects.

transcript.speaker: Hannah Ostrowski
transcript.text: Honestly, if that spreadsheet dies I'll throw a party. Longer term I keep daydreaming about cohort-retention analytics for the newsletter side, but that's well past onboarding.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: It's a good daydream — the modeling work we're doing now is exactly the foundation for it. Nothing we need to change in the plan.

transcript.speaker: Hannah Ostrowski
transcript.text: That's what I hoped. And team-wise, the analysts are excited. Nervous about dbt, but excited.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: Nervous-but-excited is the ideal starting state — the training session in the plan is built for exactly that.

transcript.speaker: Hannah Ostrowski
transcript.text: Good to know. Nothing else from me — mostly wanted to put faces to names.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: Mission accomplished then. Everything concrete stays as scheduled from kickoff — speak at the weekly.
